This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum
 Oral Judgment
(Per: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum)
This appeal is by the claimants for having lost their son in a road traffic accident dated 15.4.2012.

The appellants who are the parents admit that the deceased along with others was traveling in a goods vehicle bearing No.MH 13/AX.2339 while the offending truck bearing No.KA.36/A.2976 was illegally parked in the middle of the NC: 2024:KHC-K:9754 road.

Therefore, the appellants contended that the accident occurred due to reckless parking by the driver of the offending truck bearing Regn.No.KA.36/A.2976.
2.

The Tribunal referring to the charge sheet materials apportioned negligence in the ratio of 30:70 i.e. 70% negligence was attributed to the driver of the goods truck bearing No.MH.13/AX.2339 and 30% to the driver of the offending truck bearing No.KA.36/A.2976, who had illegally parked the truck in the middle of the road.
3. The Tribunal having apportioned the negligence dismissed the claim petition against respondent No.4/New India Insurance company on the ground it is not liable to pay 70% of compensation since the inmates of the goods vehicle were traveling as gratuitous passengers.

The claim petition was in fact allowed against the owner of the offending truck i.e. respondent No.3 and 30% liability was fastened on respondents 1 and 2 primarily fixing the liability on respondent No.2/Oriental Sultan vs Mohammed Hanif on 9 December, 2024

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170854429/
2 Insurance Company Limited.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:9754 4.

Heard the learned counsel for the appellants/claimants and the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2/Oriental Insurance Company as well as the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.4/New India Assurance Company limited.
5.
In the present case, since two vehicles are involved, the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the claimants has advanced arguments seeking to invoke the doctrine of composite negligence.

It is contended that the second respondent, Oriental Insurance Company, which provided insurance coverage to the offending truck bearing No.KA.36/A.2976, bears a significant share of responsibility for the accident.
The truck in question, was negligently and unlawfully parked in the middle of the road, thereby contributing to the collision.
The counsel has urged this Court to hold Oriental Insurance Company liable for the claim amount.

Furthermore, the counsel has requested that the insurance company be directed to first compensate the claimants and subsequently recover the NC:
2024:KHC-K:9754 amount from the third respondent, who is the registered owner of the offending truck bearing No.MH.13/AX.2339.
This approach, it is argued, would ensure fair and timely compensation to the victims while preserving the rights of the insurer to seek redress against the negligent truck owner.

6. Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company placing reliance on the latest judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Balu Krishna Chavan .vs. Reliance General Insurance Company1 would point out that even if it is the case of composite negligence, having regard to the fact that both the tortfeasors are made party to the claim petition, the Insurance Company which has insured the offending truck bearing No.KA.36/A.2976, which had parked in the middle of the road cannot be called upon to satisfy the entire compensation.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:9754 7.

entities.text: Balu Krishna Chavan .vs. Reliance General Insurance Company1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: FINDING ON NEGLIGENCE:

On meticulous examination of the records, this Court is of the view that negligence fixed in the ratio of 70:30 runs contrary to the records as well as the judgment rendered by the Apex Court in the case of Archit Saini vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd2.

entities.text: Archit Saini vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand, two heavy goods vehicles are involved in the accident.
This accident has occurred at 7.45 a.m.

Primarily, the driver of the goods vehicle bearing No.KA 36 A 2976 was grossly responsible for recklessly parking the vehicle in the middle of the road while the driver of the goods truck bearing No.MH 13 AX 2339 in gross violation of the policy conditions has allowed around 30 inmates to travel in the goods vehicle when there is clear bar to carry passengers in a goods vehicle.
The driver of the offending truck in which all these inmates were proceeding was also negligent in not taking appropriate precautions having found the truck parked in the middle of the road.

In the 2018(3) SCC 365 NC: 2024:KHC-K:9754 Sultan vs Mohammed Hanif on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170854429/
3 light of the law laid down by the Apex Court, the driver of the truck bearing No.KA 36 A 2976 was also equally responsible in illegally parking the goods vehicle in the middle of the road.

entities.text: 2018(3) SCC 365 NC: 2024:KHC-K:9754 Sultan vs Mohammed Hanif
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Therefore, the negligence apportioned in the ratio of 70:30 appears to be contrary to the records.

This Court on independent review of the materials on record is of the view that both the drivers were negligent and therefore, the negligence has to be attributed in the ratio of 50:50.
9.
The principles of composite negligence as argued by the learned counsel for the claimants is not available as the claimants have rightly decided to include both the tortfeasors.

When both the tortfeasors are before the Court, the Oriental Insurance Company which had issued the policy cover to the goods vehicle bearing No.KA.36/A.2976 cannot be called upon to satisfy the entire award when the Insurance company and the owner NC: 2024:KHC-K:9754 of the vehicle in which the inmates were proceeding are also party to the claim petition.

10. Therefore the theory of pay and recovery to call upon respondent No.2/Oriental Insurance Company to satisfy the award and then recover the same either from respondent No.4/New India Insurance Company or respondent No.3, who are insurer and owner of offending truck bearing No.MH-13-AX-2339 which was illegally carrying the passengers cannot be accepted.

Respondent No.3, who is the owner of the offending truck bearing No. MH-13-AX-2339 is liable to deposit 50%
of the compensation awarded.

Respondent No.2/Insurance Company who is the insurer of the goods vehicle bearing No. KA.36/A.2976 which was illegally parked is jointly and severally liable along with respondent No.1 to deposit 50% of the compensation awarded.

11. FINDING ON QUANTUM:
Claimants are the parents who are asserting that they have lost their son, who according to them was NC: 2024:KHC-K:9754 earning Rs.6,000/- per month.
The Tribunal in absence of income proof has assessed the income at Rs.3,000/- and has awarded Rs.4,09,000/- with 9% interest per annum.
12. This Court having independently assessed the records is of the view that the income assessed at Rs.3,000/- is on the lower side.
In absence of income proof, if the income chart is examined, the KSLSA has notionally prescribed the income at Rs.6,500/- p.m.
However, in the claim petition, the claimants have specifically contended that the deceased was earning Rs.6,000/- per month.
Therefore, accepting the income as pleaded in the claim petition, the income is notionally assessed at Rs.6,000/-.
Adding 40% towards future prospects, the income is assessed at Rs.8,400/-.

After deducting 50%, the income is assessed at Rs.4,200/- and applying the multiplier of 18,
compensation re-determined under the head of loss of dependency works out to Rs.9,07,200/-.

- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9754 Sultan vs Mohammed Hanif on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170854429/
4 13.
Under conventional heads, the claimants are entitled to Rs.1,10,000/-.

Additionally, 10%
escalation for every three years is awarded on the conventional heads applying the principles laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors3.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, Rs.22,000/- additional amount is awarded under the conventional heads.

Hence, the total compensation re-determined by this Court works out Rs.10,39,200/- as against Rs.4,09,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the enhanced compensation works out to Rs.6,30,200/-, which the appellants are held entitled with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

6. For the foregoing reasons, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
2017 ACJ 2700 SC - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9754 (ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 19.12.2018 passed by the Tribunal in MVC.No.926/2012 is hereby modified.

(iii) The appellants/claimants are held entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.6,30,200/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
(iv) The negligence is fixed in the ratio of 50:50 on the drivers of both the vehicles.

Respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally held liable to deposit 50% of compensation awarded and balance 50%
shall be paid by respondent No.3/Owner of the truck i.e. MH- 13-AX-2339.
(v) The order of the Tribunal insofar as apportionment remains unaltered.
(vi) The amount in deposit shall be remitted to the Tribunal to enable the claimants to withdraw the same.

SD/-
(SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM) JUDGE ALB Sultan vs Mohammed Hanif on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170854429/
